title: Query count for the disjoint completion procedure
statement: Let $R_1,R_2,B_3$ be finite sets of coordinates in an $n$-coordinate cube, with $R_1$ disjoint from $R_2\cup B_3$ and $R_2$ disjoint from $B_3$. For each sign, let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be decision trees querying coordinates from $R_1$ and $R_2$, respectively, and let $E_3$ be a decision tree querying coordinates from $B_3$. Fix a sign $x_1$ and an input $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$. The query count of the combined procedure is the query count of $C_1(x_1)$ plus the following: if $C_1(x_1)$ evaluates to $x_1$, add the query count of $C_2(x_1)$ and then add zero if $C_2(x_1)$ evaluates to the value of $C_1(x_1)$, or otherwise add the query count of $E_3$; if $C_1(x_1)$ does not evaluate to $x_1$, add the query count of $E_3$ and then add zero if $E_3$ evaluates to the value of $C_1(x_1)$, or otherwise add the query count of $C_2(x_1)$.
hypotheses_covered: $R_1,R_2,B_3$ are finite subsets of the $n$ coordinates
$C_1$ maps each sign to a decision tree on $R_1$
$C_2$ maps each sign to a decision tree on $R_2$
